gap: No result ChatGPT got states how long each bank can actually keep up 140 W before it throttles. Smartzone.de measured the Anker Prime 26K 300W at 140 W for 35 minutes, about 82 Wh at full speed, before it dropped to 60 W at 10% charge. Its 280 W two-laptop mode lasted only 13 minutes before falling to 100 W. Techtest.org found UGREEN's 165W 25K delivers only about half its capacity at 140 W, roughly 16 minutes, before dropping to 65 W.
standout_why: I read the Wirecutter page through the proxy ChatGPT got. It lists only rated mAh, port watts, weight and price for the Anker Prime A110A ($230, 1.3 lb, about 97 Wh). It has no measured delivered Wh, no time at full power and no cost per Wh. ChatGPT's own answers say 'fast enough for two laptops simultaneously' and '300W total' with no duration, so none of its shown text has the throttling numbers. WIRED would not load (fetch blocked), and I did not open the Popular Science or Expert Reviews pages. Expert Reviews' separate Prime A110A review only says the reviewer 'suspected' throttling, with no minutes or watts. I scored this 2 rather than 3 because I could not check WIRED.
decides: It confirms the Anker Prime 26K as the laptop fast-charging pick: it is the only candidate measured holding 140 W through almost all of its charge (35 min, about 82 Wh). It also undercuts ChatGPT's 'two laptops at once' line, because 280 W lasts 13 minutes and then drops to 100 W combined. For value, the UGREEN 145W 25K has the lowest cost per delivered Wh ($1.26) and the most Wh per lb (71). But in Techtest.org's test its top single port was 100 W, which dropped to 65 W at about 29% charge. That makes it a better-value phone, tablet and MacBook Air bank, not a sustained 140 W one. The UGREEN 165W 25K costs less per Wh than the Anker ($1.48 vs $2.57) but holds 140 W for only about 16 minutes.
